result.summary: Makes the default combined fee estimator in `estimatesmartfee` fall back to the `block_policy` estimate whenever the mempool estimator is unavailable, returning an error only if the block policy estimate also fails. Changes the mempool estimator to return an error rather than the relay fee floor when the mempool is too sparse to fill block-template percentiles, and clears tracked mined-block stats if loading the mempool from disk fails at startup. Also renames the default estimator parameter in `estimatesmartfee` and the internal enum from "none" to "auto", keeping "none" as an accepted alias.
result.problem: When the mempool is sparse or empty (such as after a restart without persistence or when mempool.dat is corrupt), the mempool estimator previously returned the fee floor, causing severe underestimation. In other states where the mempool estimator was not ready (during startup, during mempool loading, or under low block coverage), the combined estimator returned an error instead of falling back to valid block policy estimates.
evidence: The PR description explains that when the mempool is empty or sparse, returning the fee floor 'can be a significant underestimation, since the now-missing mempool may have held much higher-feerate transactions.'

Commit 697d1b7127 explains that without clearing mined-block stats on failed mempool loads, 'the estimator would keep a window describing a mempool the node no longer has and, once the mempool refilled, serve an estimate built on it.'
result.changed_since_previous: Added a commit that renames the RPC `fee_rate_estimator` default option and internal enum enumerator from "none" to "auto", preserving backward compatibility by mapping unknown strings and "none" to "auto".
result.card: Makes the default combined fee estimator in estimatesmartfee fall back to the block policy estimate whenever the mempool estimator cannot produce an estimate, rather than returning an error. It changes the mempool estimator to return an error instead of the minimum relay fee floor when the mempool is too sparse to fill block percentiles, preventing severe fee underestimation on nodes with empty or sparse mempools. In addition, when mempool loading fails at startup, the estimator clears its mined-block window to avoid serving estimates based on stale mempool state, and renames the combined estimator option in RPC from 'none' to 'auto'.

risk.why: Flaws in fee rate estimation logic could cause wallets relying on estimatesmartfee to underpay or overpay transaction fees, resulting in delayed confirmations or excessive costs.
